title: Making crane feathers in CLO3D!
content:
Hi! I urgently need to make feathers for an outfit I'm making, but don't know how to use Blender - so importing an OBJ in is out of the question. I've been trying to make feathers using fabric and the fur preset, but I can't achieve the right look at all... 

If anyone has any ideas or could give me a tutorial, please do! 😳 I've attached my failed feather attempts along with the type of feather I'm trying to create.![e2708e868f5f4842ae962be95f753550](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/933b4d9220d64894b28345ef3541a753/images/e2708e868f5f4842ae962be95f75355071b4cd30-44c6-4f35-b05a-a17d7734e772_600.jpg)![6061d374baa741bbbc6559af64cca561](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/933b4d9220d64894b28345ef3541a753/images/6061d374baa741bbbc6559af64cca561failedfeathers.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I would make fabric stripes, place feather as a graphic and then set the fabric opacity to 0

Comment 2: - I see a feather like this on Turbosquid for $1 when sorting by price.- I don't think it's impossible to create a feather this way in CLO, but it will require different furs applied to several separate pattern pieces and variation within the fur length.- Is using that image you have and faking the feathers with maps an option?
content_description: A community-driven page seeking advice and tutorials on creating realistic feathers in Blender without importing external models.

title: Missing all V1 Fabrics after installed the new version 2025.0252 (r54232). Crossed check another user their same version still have all of V1 fabrics.
content:
![20b936fc774b4c6b969952377b314497](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/45b8632cfb1e44798b58c08adcbbbaba/images/20b936fc774b4c6b969952377b314497Screenshot%202025-05-20%20at%2019.36.00.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: HiIf you want to have V1 fabrics again, these may be:Ask another user to send you the V1 fabric folder (eg Route:Documents \ Co \ Assets \ Fabric \ v1)

Comment 2: Hi, all V1 fabrics were removed as the V2 fabrics have been digitized in the current method and are more accurate in simulation. The other user probably still has them because the fabrics are still stored in their local assets. If yours is a fresh installation, they would not be included.
Reply 1: Hi ok noted, thank you for the reply.

title: Shirring - What am I doing Wrong?
content:
Hey Clo Community!

I am working on a chemise with shirring along the neckline. I tried to use the shirring tool and adjust the interval/height but nothing is happening to my garment when I turn the simulation on. I've tried changing the simulation type, particle distance, and general resolution of the garment but it just continues to remain flat. This is what my windows look like:![2dc6f28072f444b7b270d9b0bcab2ff2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/c5b22a33194d4149a80993ad6f2b481f/images/2dc6f28072f444b7b270d9b0bcab2ff2image.png)And this is a sketch of what I am trying to achieve:

![e452654beda34dd49ca9f96fa11eb533](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202505/c5b22a33194d4149a80993ad6f2b481f/images/e452654beda34dd49ca9f96fa11eb533image.png)What am I doing wrong....

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you!

Comment 2: The comment from Veronika is correct. There is currently nothing applied to actually pull in/gather the material together. Applying Elastic to the top edge and then reducing the percentage amount will help to begin the gatering

Comment 3: Hi! I personally havent worked with shirring, but I can suggest that first you need to add an elastic to this part and the shirring, it will make it more detailed.
content_description: A community support page to troubleshoot and resolve issues with applying shirring effects in Clo 3D garment simulations.
